s1.syndrome_frame: A young adult with a systolic murmur and abnormal cardiac structure and function
salient_findings: Systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region
Complete right bundle-branch block on ECG
Dilated right atrium and right ventricle on echocardiography
key_facts: 29-year-old primigravida woman
No history of dyspnea, chest pain, palpitation, or lower limb swelling
Vital parameters within normal limits
Systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region
Normal sinus rhythm with heart rate of 70 beats/min on ECG
Complete right bundle-branch block with normal PR interval on ECG
Fragmented QRS with a notch on the R wave in inferior leads on ECG
No significant ST-T segment changes on ECG
Dilated right atrium and right ventricle on transthoracic echocardiography
Large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt on transthoracic echocardiography
Normal cardiac output on right-sided heart catheterization
Step-up in oxygenation from superior vena cava to right atrium
Pulmonary vascular resistance: 1.8 Wood units

raw.rationale: The presence of a large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt, dilated right atrium and right ventricle, and a step-up in oxygenation from the superior vena cava to the right atrium are consistent with an ostium secundum atrial septal defect.

rejected.why: Not directly supported by the findings of a large defect with left-to-right shunt and dilated right atrium and ventricle

rejected.label: Ventricular septal defect
rejected.why: The location of the murmur and the echocardiography findings suggest an atrial septal defect rather than a ventricular septal defect

rejected.label: Atrial septal defect
rejected.why: Too broad, as the case specifics point more precisely to an ostium secundum type
